sections.html:
Every operation is one HTTP request to the API's endpoint. A body, in a request or a response, is JSON. The commands here read the endpoint from EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT:

export EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT='https://<endpoint>'

Send these headers:

HeaderValueOn
Content-Typeapplication/jsona request with a JSON body
Example-Versionv1every request

Example-Version names the release this reference documents. A request without it is refused with HTTP 400, except for a sender-signed operation, which is served at the current release.
sections.markdown:
Every operation is one HTTP request to the API's endpoint. A body, in a request or a response, is JSON. The commands here read the endpoint from `EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT`:

```sh
export EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT='https://<endpoint>'
```

Send these headers:

| Header | Value | On |
|---|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | a request with a JSON body |
| `Example-Version` | `v1` | every request |

`Example-Version` names the release this reference documents. A request without it is refused with HTTP 400, except for a sender-signed operation, which is served at the current release.
sections.title: Send a request

sections.html:
Ping is GET /ping:

curl "$EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT"'/ping' \
  -H 'Example-Version: v1'

It answers 200 with a JSON body:

{
  "ok": false
}

Every operation's page has its request, its response and a command like this one.
sections.markdown:
`Ping` is `GET /ping`:

```sh
curl "$EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT"'/ping' \
  -H 'Example-Version: v1'
```

It answers `200` with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "ok": false
}
```

sections.html:
Each of the API's simple types is written in JSON like this:

API typeJSON
booleantrue or false

A structure is an object with a member for each of its members. Leave an optional member out to send nothing for it. In a path, a query string or a header, a value is written as text.
